verdict.rationale: Blaxel's own docs describe hosted cloud sandboxes built for running code. AI-generated code therefore runs on Blaxel's infrastructure rather than yours, and you can run shell commands and processes inside it. The docs also describe dropping privileges to an unprivileged user and egress allowlists or denylists that prevent data exfiltration, which together cover executing untrusted code without exposing your own systems. missing for 10: documentation of the underlying isolation boundary (e.g., microVM or kernel-level separation between tenants), independent or hands-on corroboration of the sandbox security claims.

support.subject: As a developer, I can execute untrusted, AI-generated code without risking my own infrastructure

citations.quote: Execute and manage processes in your sandboxes with Blaxel SDK. Run shell commands, retrieve process information, and control process execution.
Scope everything a sandbox runs on your behalf to an unprivileged user while the sandbox API keeps the privileges it needs.
Restrict which external domains, HTTP methods, and URL paths a Blaxel sandbox can reach using allowlists and denylists to prevent data exfiltration and unwanted outbound traffic.
